# **NFS2 file specs** #

*Last time updated: 2026-10-26 18:01:28.434061+00:00*

*Generated by [TailsLab](../README.md) from its parser code.*


# **Info by file extensions** #

**\*.BNK** sound bank. [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)

**GAMEDATA/AUDIO/PC/\*.ASF** song, **GAMEDATA/AUDIO/PC/\*.MUS** interactive music. [EaAudioStreams](#eaaudiostreams)

**GAMEDATA/AUDIO/PC/\*.MAP** interactive music map of the `.MUS` file of the same name. [EaMusicMap](#eamusicmap)

**\*.COL** track additional data. [MapColFile](#mapcolfile)
        
**\*.GEO** car 3D model. [GeoGeometry](#geogeometry)
        
**\*.FFN** bitmap font. [FfnFont](#ffnfont)

**\*.FSH** image archive. [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock)

**\*.MSK** archive with some data. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

**\*.QFS** image archive. [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock), [compressed](eac_compressions.md)

**\*.TRK** main track file. [TrkMap](#trkmap)

**GAMEDATA/TRACKS/PC/TR\<nn\>.HRZ** sky of a track for the software renderer, plain text. [Nfs2HorizonInfo](#nfs2horizoninfo)

**\*.UV** video, I just use ffmpeg to convert it

**\*.VIV** archive with some data. [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)

Did not find what you need or some given data is wrong? Please submit an
[issue](https://github.com/AndyGura/nfs-resources-converter/issues/new)


# **Block specs** #
## **Archives** ##
### **ShpiBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A container of images and palettes for them ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SHPI" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this SHPI block in bytes |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **shpi_dir** | 4 | UTF-8 string | One of: "LN32", "GIMX", "WRAP". The purpose is unknown |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*8 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: 8-bytes record, first 4 bytes is a UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian) | An array of items, each of them represents name of SHPI item (image or palette) and offset to item data in file, relatively to SHPI block start (where resource id string is presented). Names are not always unique |
| 16 + num_items\*8 | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*8 + up to the first item offset | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets to some of the entries are defined in `items_descr` block. Between them there can be non-indexed entries (palettes and texts). Possible item types:<br/>- [EacImage](#eacimage)<br/>- [EacPalette](#eacpalette) |
### **BigfBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A block-container with various data: image archives, GEO geometries, sound banks, other BIGF blocks... ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BIGF" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The length of this BIGF block in bytes. NFS6 stores the length without padding between items: header plus item lengths |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*9..? | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item type: [BigfItemDescriptionBlock](#bigfitemdescriptionblock) | Descriptions of items: offset, length and name of each of them |
| 16 + num_items\*9..? | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*9 + up to the first item offset..? | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets and lengths are defined in previous block. Possible item types:<br/>- [GeoGeometry](#geogeometry)<br/>- [ShpiBlock](#shpiblock), can be compressed like QFS file<br/>- [BigfBlock](#bigfblock)<br/>- [EaSoundBank](#easoundbank)<br/>- pure TGA image |
### **BigfItemDescriptionBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 9..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Description of a single item of BIGF archive ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of item data, relative to BIGF block start |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of item data in bytes |
| 8 | **name** | 1..? | Null-terminated UTF-8 string. Ends with first occurrence of zero byte | Item name (file name). Used as file name when the archive is unpacked |
### **EaSoundBank** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound bank "BNKl" (*.BNK of NFS2, NFS2 SE, NFS3, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6): a table of sound patches, then their wave data. Car banks (NFS2 `<car>.BNK` / `O<car>.BNK` (opponent) / `S<car>.BNK`, NFS3 `car.bnk` / `ocar.bnk` / `scar.bnk` in car.viv, NFS4 `careng.bnk` / `ocareng.bnk` / `scareng.bnk`, NFS3/NFS4 `GENCAR.BNK`, traffic `TRUCK.BNK`...) use indices 0 and 1 for the engine (looped), 2 for a one-shot with random detune range 200-250 (gear shift, like `gear` of TNFS car banks) and 3 for the horn (looped). Opponent banks have the engine and the horn only: NFS2 `O<car>.BNK` in slots 0 and 1 of a 2-slot table, NFS3 `ocar.bnk` / NFS4 `ocareng.bnk` in slots 0 and 3. NFS4 `careng.bnk` has more engine samples at higher indices (presumably one per RPM range). `W*.BNK` of NFS2 SE are car speech ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "BNKl" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 2 (NFS2, NFS2 SE, most of NFS3 GameData/Audio/SFX), 4 (NFS3 car.viv, NFS4, NFS5, NFS6) or 5 (NFS6) |
| 6 | **num_items** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of slots in `items_descr` |
| 8 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 2 and 4: offset of the wave data, i.e. the length of the table and the patches. Version 5: file length |
| 12 | **wave_data_length** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Version 4: length of the wave data. Version 5: 0 |
| 12..16 | **unk0** | 0..4 | Optional (if version >= 4): 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 12..20 | **items_descr** | num_items\*4 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset of every patch, relative to its own position in this table, the array index being the sample index used by the game. 0 is an empty slot |
| 12 + num_items\*4..20 + num_items\*4 | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | Sound patches ([EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch)) at the offsets of `items_descr`, then wave data |
## **Geometries** ##
### **GeoGeometry** ###
#### **Size**: 1804..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A set of 3D meshes, used for cars and props. Contains multiple meshes with high details, medium and low LOD-s. Textures are in a separate QFS archive: <name>.QFS next to the GEO file (NFS2), or CARMODEL/PC/<name>.QFS for GEO items of CARDATA.VIV (NFS2SE) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 4 | **unk1** | 128 | Array of `32` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 132 | **unk2** | 8 | 8-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 140 | **parts** | 1664..? | Array of `32` items<br/>Item type: [GeoMesh](#geomesh) | Array of 32 body parts: 20 high poly, 3 medium poly, 3 low poly and 6 reserved spaces. Description of each of them:<br/>0: High-Poly Additional Body Part<br/>1: High-Poly Main Body Part<br/>2: High-Poly Ground Part<br/>3: High-Poly Front Part<br/>4: High-Poly Back Part<br/>5: High-Poly Left Side Part<br/>6: High-Poly Right Side Part<br/>7: High-Poly Additional Left Side Part<br/>8: High-Poly Additional Right Side Part<br/>9: High-Poly Spoiler Part<br/>10: High-Poly Additional Part<br/>11: High-Poly Backlights<br/>12: High-Poly Front Right Wheel<br/>13: High-Poly Front Right Wheel Part<br/>14: High-Poly Front Left Wheel<br/>15: High-Poly Front Left Wheel Part<br/>16: High-Poly Rear Right Wheel<br/>17: High-Poly Rear Right Wheel Part<br/>18: High-Poly Rear Left Wheel<br/>19: High-Poly Rear Left Wheel Part<br/>20: Medium-Poly Additional Body Part<br/>21: Medium-Poly Main Body Part<br/>22: Medium-Poly Ground Part<br/>23: Low-Poly Wheel Part<br/>24: Low-Poly Main Part<br/>25: Low-Poly Side Part<br/> |
### **GeoMesh** ###
#### **Size**: 52..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A single mesh, can use multiple textures ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_vrtx** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | number of vertices in block |
| 4 | **num_plgn** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | number of polygons in block |
| 8 | **pos** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | position of part in 3d space (pivot of the mesh, vertices are relative to it). The unit is meter |
| 20 | **unk0** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 24 | **unk1** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 28 | **unk2** | 8 | 8-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0x0 | Unknown purpose |
| 36 | **unk3** | 8 | 8-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0x1 | Unknown purpose |
| 44 | **unk4** | 8 | 8-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0x1 | Unknown purpose |
| 52 | **vertices** | num_vrtx\*6 | Array of `num_vrtx` items<br/>Item size: 6 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Vertex coordinates. The unit is meter |
| 52 + num_vrtx\*6 | **offset** | up to offset 52 + ceil(num_vrtx/2)\*12 | Padding bytes | Data offset, happens when `num_vrtx` is odd |
| 52 + ceil(num_vrtx/2)\*12 | **polygons** | num_plgn\*12 | Array of `num_plgn` items<br/>Item type: [GeoPolygon](#geopolygon) | Array of mesh polygons |
### **GeoPolygon** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A single polygon of the mesh. Texture coordinates seem to be hardcoded in game:for triangles `[[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1]]` if "uv_flip" else `[[0, 1], [1, 1], [1, 0]]`, for quads `[[0, 1], [1, 1], [1, 0], [0, 0]]` if "uv_flip" else `[[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1]]` ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **mapping** | 1 | 8 flags container<br/><details><summary>flag names (from least to most significant)</summary>0: is_triangle<br/>1: uv_flip<br/>2: flip_normal<br/>4: double_sided</details> | Polygon properties. "is_triangle" means that 3th and 4th vertices in the polygon are the same, "uv_flip" changes texture coordinates, "flip normal" inverts normal vector of the polygon, "double-sided" makes polygon visible from the other side. |
| 1 | **unk0** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 4 | **vertex_indices** | 4 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Indexes of vertices |
| 8 | **texture_name** | 4 | UTF-8 string | ID of texture from neighbouring QFS file |
## **Maps** ##
### **TrkMap** ###
#### **Size**: 32..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Main track file. The track is split into blocks (segments), grouped by 8 into superblocks. Each block has a terrain mesh at 3 resolutions and extrablocks with props. Polygon texture values index the textures_map extrablock of the accompanying COL file, which points to images in <track>0.QFS ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "TRAC" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **unk0** | 20 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 24 | **num_superblocks** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of superblocks (nsblk) |
| 28 | **num_blocks** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of blocks (nblk) |
| 32 | **superblock_offsets** | num_superblocks\*4 | Array of `num_superblocks` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset to each of the superblocks |
| 32 + num_superblocks\*4 | **block_positions** | num_blocks\*12 | Array of `num_blocks` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Positions of blocks in the world: a point on the road at the start of each block. Block vertices are relative to these points, and all positions together form the track path (closed loop) |
| 32 + num_superblocks\*4 + num_blocks\*12 | **skip_bytes** | up to offset superblock_offsets[0] | Padding bytes | Useless padding |
| superblock_offsets[0] | **superblocks** | num_superblocks\*12..? | Array of `num_superblocks` items<br/>Item type: [TrkSuperBlock](#trksuperblock) | Superblocks |
### **TrkSuperBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A group of up to 8 consecutive track blocks ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Superblock size in bytes |
| 4 | **num_blocks** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of blocks in this superblock. Usually 8 or less in the last superblock |
| 8 | **unk** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 12 | **block_offsets** | num_blocks\*4 | Array of `num_blocks` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset to each of the blocks |
| 12 + num_blocks\*4 | **blocks** | num_blocks\*88..? | Array of `num_blocks` items<br/>Item type: [TrkBlock](#trkblock) | Blocks |
### **TrkBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 88..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Track block (NFS2, NFS2 SE): a segment of the track (8 slices of the COL collision data) with terrain mesh at 3 resolutions, the road polygons the physics uses and extrablocks (props, lanes, road vectors etc.). Vertex coordinates are relative to the block position, defined in `block_positions` of the track file. The polygon records after the vertices are 6 consecutive sets: `polygons` (3 levels of detail), `extra_polygons`, `road_polygons` and `unk_polygons`. NFS2 SE keeps the raw block bytes in memory (track reader nfs2sen.exe 0x461b00..) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block size in bytes |
| 4 | **block_size_2** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block size in bytes (duplicated) |
| 8 | **num_extrablocks** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of extrablocks |
| 10 | **first_slice** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Index of the block's first slice (track collision spline point) in the `collision_data` extrablock of the COL file: `block_idx` * 8 in every NFS2 and NFS2 SE track. NFS2 SE reads it as a signed 16-bit value (nfs2sen.exe 0x461b30) |
| 12 | **block_idx** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block index (serial number) |
| 16 | **bounds** | 48 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Block bounding rectangle |
| 64 | **extrablocks_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An offset to "extrablock_offsets" block from here |
| 68 | **nv8** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of stick-to-next vertices: vertices shared with the next block, stored relative to the position of the next block |
| 70 | **nv4** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of own vertices for 1/4 resolution |
| 72 | **nv2** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of own vertices for 1/2 resolution |
| 74 | **nv1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of own vertices for full resolution. Vertex sets of lower resolutions are subsets of it: nv4 <= nv2 <= nv1 |
| 76 | **np4** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons for 1/4 resolution |
| 78 | **np2** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons for 1/2 resolution |
| 80 | **np1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons for full resolution |
| 82 | **num_extra_polygons** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons in `extra_polygons` |
| 84 | **num_road_polygons** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons in `road_polygons` |
| 86 | **num_unk_polygons** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons in `unk_polygons` (0..16 in the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks) |
| 88 | **vertices** | (nv8+nv1)\*6 | Array of `nv8+nv1` items<br/>Item size: 6 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Vertices. The first nv8 items are relative to the position of the next block (`block_positions[block_idx + 1]`, or of block 0 for the last block), the remaining nv1 items are relative to the position of this block |
| 88 + (nv8+nv1)\*6 | **polygons** | (np4+np2+np1)\*8 | Array of `np4+np2+np1` items<br/>Item type: [ColPolygon](#colpolygon) | Polygons: np4 polygons of the 1/4 resolution mesh, then np2 polygons of the 1/2 resolution mesh, then np1 polygons of the full resolution mesh. The three sets are alternative levels of detail of the same terrain; the converter exports the full resolution one. Vertex indexes point to `vertices` |
| 88 + (nv8+nv1)\*6 + (np4+np2+np1)\*8 | **extra_polygons** | num_extra_polygons\*8 | Array of `num_extra_polygons` items<br/>Item type: [ColPolygon](#colpolygon) | A 4th polygon set, purpose unknown. NFS2 SE keeps a pointer to it per loaded block (slot loader nfs2sen.exe 0x437420) |
| 88 + (nv8+nv1)\*6 + (np4+np2+np1)\*8 + num_extra_polygons\*8 | **road_polygons** | num_road_polygons\*8 | Array of `num_road_polygons` items<br/>Item type: [ColPolygon](#colpolygon) | The road surface polygons the physics searches for the polygon under a car (NFS2 SE: nfs2sen.exe 0x4384c0, pointer set by the slot loader 0x437420). `median_polygons` records point to runs of them per slice, `polygon_map` has one record per polygon of this set (road vector and surface). Vertex indexes point to `vertices`, so indexes below nv8 are vertices of the next block |
| 88 + (nv8+nv1)\*6 + (np4+np2+np1)\*8 + num_extra_polygons\*8 + num_road_polygons\*8 | **unk_polygons** | num_unk_polygons\*8 | Array of `num_unk_polygons` items<br/>Item type: [ColPolygon](#colpolygon) | A 6th set of polygon records (vertex indexes within `vertices`), purpose unknown. The NFS2 SE slot loader (nfs2sen.exe 0x437420) only computes where it starts (the end of `road_polygons`) |
| 88 + (nv8+nv1)\*6 + (np4+np2+np1)\*8 + num_extra_polygons\*8 + num_road_polygons\*8 + num_unk_polygons\*8 | **padding** | up to offset extrablocks_offset + 64 | Padding bytes | 0 or 2 bytes up to `extrablock_offsets`. In NFS2 SE zeros, which align `extrablock_offsets` to 4 bytes from the block start; some NFS2 blocks have other bytes here |
| extrablocks_offset + 64 | **extrablock_offsets** | num_extrablocks\*4 | Array of `num_extrablocks` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset to each of the extrablocks |
| extrablocks_offset + 64 + num_extrablocks\*4 | **extrablocks_bytes** | block_size-local_offset | Bytes | A part of block, where extrablocks data is located. Offsets to the entries are defined in `extrablock_offsets` block. Item type:<br/>- [ColExtraBlock](#colextrablock) |
### **MapColFile** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Track additional data (COL file), a list of extrablocks: textures map (used by polygons of the TRK file), track-wide props with their 3D models and collision data (road centre line for the physics engine) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "COLL" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **unk** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0xb | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | File size in bytes |
| 12 | **num_extrablocks** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of extrablocks |
| 16 | **extrablock_offsets** | num_extrablocks\*4 | Array of `num_extrablocks` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset to each of the extrablocks |
| 16 + num_extrablocks\*4 | **extrablocks_bytes** | block_size-16-4\*num_extrablocks | Bytes | A part of block, where extra blocks data is located. Offsets are defined in previous "extrablock_offsets" field. Item type:<br/>- [ColExtraBlock](#colextrablock) |
### **ColExtraBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A typed container of data records. The same structure is used for extrablocks inside TRK blocks and in the COL file; record type is defined by `type` ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block size in bytes |
| 4 | **type** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>2 (0x2): textures_map<br/>4 (0x4): block_numbers<br/>5 (0x5): polygon_map<br/>6 (0x6): median_polygons<br/>7 (0x7): props_7<br/>8 (0x8): prop_descriptions<br/>9 (0x9): lanes<br/>11 (0xb): track_objects<br/>13 (0xd): road_vectors<br/>15 (0xf): collision_data<br/>18 (0x12): props_18<br/>19 (0x13): props_19</details> | Type of the data records. textures_map, props_7, prop_descriptions and collision_data are found in COL file; polygon_map, block_numbers, median_polygons, props_18, prop_descriptions, lanes, track_objects and road_vectors in TRK blocks. NFS2 and NFS2 SE TRK blocks also have types 10, 14 and 17 (meaning unknown, kept as raw bytes) |
| 5 | **unk** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x0 | Unknown purpose |
| 6 | **num_data_records** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of data records |
| 8 | **data_records** | ? | Type according to enum `type`:<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [TexturesMapExtraDataRecord](#texturesmapextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [PolygonMapExtraDataRecord](#polygonmapextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [MedianExtraDataRecord](#medianextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [PropExtraDataRecord](#propextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [PropDescriptionExtraDataRecord](#propdescriptionextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [LanesExtraDataRecord](#lanesextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [TrackObjectExtraDataRecord](#trackobjectextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [RoadVectorsExtraDataRecord](#roadvectorsextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [CollisionExtraDataRecord](#collisionextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [PropExtraDataRecord](#propextradatarecord)<br/>- Array of `num_data_records` items<br/>Item type: [PropExtraDataRecord](#propextradatarecord)<br/>- Bytes | Data records, block class picked according to `type`. Records of unknown types are kept as raw bytes |
### **TexturesMapExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 10 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Texture reference. Polygons of the track (TRK) and of props refer to items of this table by index, the item defines the actual texture in the QFS archive and its orientation on the polygon ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **texture_number** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the texture in the track QFS file (<track>0.QFS) |
| 2 | **unk** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 3 | **alignment** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>1 (0x1): rotate_180<br/>3 (0x3): rotate_270<br/>5 (0x5): normal<br/>9 (0x9): rotate_90<br/>16 (0x10): flip_v<br/>18 (0x12): rotate_270_2<br/>20 (0x14): flip_h<br/>24 (0x18): rotate_90_2</details> | Orientation of the texture on the polygon, which game uses instead of UV-s. The converter uses base UV-s (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0) for the 4 polygon vertices and modifies them according to the enum value: rotate_* shift them by 1, 2 or 3 vertices, flip_h/flip_v mirror them |
| 4 | **luminosity** | 3 | Color RGB values | Luminosity color |
| 7 | **black** | 3 | Color RGB values | Unknown, usually black |
### **PolygonMapExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 2 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A record of the polygon_map extrablock (NFS2, NFS2 SE TRK blocks): road vector and surface of a polygon of the block's `road_polygons`, one record per polygon (in every block of the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **vectors_idx** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | An index of entry in road_vectors extrablock |
| 1 | **surface** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>1-bit flag "barriers"<br/>1-bit flag "objects"<br/>6-bits int "type" | Road surface byte, as NFS2 SE uses it: low 6 bits `type` the surface type, which indexes the physics' grip / surface tables; bit 0x80 `barriers`: a car standing on the polygon checks barriers (nfs2sen.exe 0x44e8e0), bit 0x40 `objects`: track objects are checked. Value 0x0e is not road: the road polygon search (0x4384c0) skips it. A polygon whose `type` is 0 is a barrier / wall for the barrier check |
### **MedianExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 8 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A record of the median_polygons extrablock (NFS2, NFS2 SE TRK blocks): the road polygons of a slice, one record per slice of the block (record index = slice - the block's `first_slice`). NFS2 SE searches the run of `road_polygons` for the polygon under a car (nfs2sen.exe 0x4384c0) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **first_polygon** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the slice's first polygon in the block's `road_polygons` |
| 2 | **num_polygons** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Number of the slice's polygons in `road_polygons`, from `first_polygon` on |
| 3 | **unk** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 2..6 in the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks |
| 4 | **alt_slice_1** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | A slice of an alternative route (track fork), -1 when none. When no polygon is found under a car, NFS2 SE retries the search from the nearer of `alt_slice_1` and `alt_slice_2` (nfs2sen.exe 0x438d80) |
| 6 | **alt_slice_2** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | A slice of another alternative route, -1 when none, used like `alt_slice_1` |
### **AnimatedPropPosition** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Animation of prop position: a sequence of keyframes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_frames** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of frames |
| 2 | **anim_delay** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Delay between frames (animation speed). Unit is not confirmed, the converter assumes 1/64 of a second |
| 4 | **frames** | num_frames\*20 | Array of `num_frames` items<br/>Item type: [AnimatedPropPositionFrame](#animatedproppositionframe) | Animation frames, played in a loop |
### **AnimatedPropPositionFrame** ###
#### **Size**: 20 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A single keyframe of animated prop movement ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Object position in 3D space |
| 12 | **orientation** | 8 | Rotation quaternion (x,y,z,w), in the same axes as the positions next to it, where each component is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 14 bits is a fractional part | Object orientation at this keyframe. Prop vertices are rotated by it (v' = q v q^-1), then moved to `position` |
### **SpecialPropPosition** ###
#### **Size**: 16 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Positioning of a special prop: a static prop which is also a track object the car collides with (NFS2, NFS2 SE TRK blocks) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Object position in 3D space |
| 12 | **special_idx** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of a record in the track_objects extrablock (type 11) of the same TRK block: the object the car collides with, at the same position. In the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks every track_objects record is referenced by exactly one special_prop of the block's props_7 |
### **PropExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: 3D model placement (prop). Same 3D model can be used few times on the track. Records of props_7 (in TRK blocks and COL file) and props_18 (in TRK blocks) extrablocks have this structure; the 3D model itself is in the prop_descriptions extrablock of the same block/file ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **block_size** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block size in bytes |
| 2 | **type** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>1 (0x1): static_prop<br/>3 (0x3): animated_prop<br/>4 (0x4): special_prop</details> | Object type. special_prop is a static prop with a reference to a track_objects record |
| 3 | **prop_descr_idx** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | An index of 3D model in "prop_descriptions" extrablock |
| 4 | **position** | ? | Type according to enum `type`:<br/>- Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part<br/>- [AnimatedPropPosition](#animatedpropposition)<br/>- [SpecialPropPosition](#specialpropposition)<br/>- Bytes | Object positioning in 3D space: a single point for static_prop, a sequence of keyframes for animated_prop. Block class picked according to `type` |
### **PropDescriptionExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: 3D model of a prop. Placed on the track by records of props_* extrablocks, which reference this model by index ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Block size in bytes |
| 4 | **num_vertices** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of vertices |
| 6 | **num_polygons** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of polygons |
| 8 | **vertices** | num_vertices\*6 | Array of `num_vertices` items<br/>Item size: 6 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Vertices, relative to the prop position |
| 8 + num_vertices\*6 | **polygons** | num_polygons\*8 | Array of `num_polygons` items<br/>Item type: [ColPolygon](#colpolygon) | Polygons. Textures are referenced through the textures_map of the COL file, the same way as for terrain polygons |
| 8 + num_vertices\*6 + num_polygons\*8 | **padding** | block_size-local_offset | Bytes | Unused space |
### **LanesExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 4 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A lane marker: ties a vertex and a polygon of the block terrain to a position on a lane ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **vertex_idx** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Vertex number (inside background 3D structure : 0 to nv1+nv8) |
| 1 | **track_pos** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Position along track inside block (0 to 7) |
| 2 | **lat_pos** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Lateral position ? (constant in each lane), -1 at the end) |
| 3 | **polygon_idx** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Polygon number (inside full-res background 3D structure : 0 to np1) |
### **TrackObjectExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 20 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A record of the track_objects extrablock (type 11, NFS2, NFS2 SE TRK blocks): a track object the car collides with, placed by a special_prop of the block (`special_idx` = record index). NFS2 SE reads the records (nfs2sen.exe 0x4383f0), collides cars with them (0x441ec0), knocks them over (0x435160) and resets their state table of 256 objects (0x435310) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Global position of the object in meters, the same as the position of the special_prop referencing it |
| 12 | **radius** | 2 | 16-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Collision radius in meters (NFS2 SE reads it as a signed 16-bit value `<< 8`, 16.16). A car hits the object when it is closer than its bounding radius + `radius`, and only if 2 * `radius` is more than the car's height above the ground. 0.035..14.09 m in the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks; for most knockable objects (947 of 980) the horizontal extent of the prop model |
| 14 | **object_idx** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Object number, the index in the game's object state table (standing / knocked away, 256 entries). In the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks the objects of a track are numbered 0..n-1 in block order |
| 16 | **height** | 1 | 8-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 1 bits is a fractional part | The top of the prop model (its highest vertex) in meters, unit 0.5 m rounded down, in every record of the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks (0.5..26 m). Its use in the game is unknown |
| 17 | **unk0** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Always 0 |
| 18 | **unk1** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | 0..16. Mostly the index of the referencing special_prop in the block's props_7 (all but 21 of the 1504 records of the NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks, the others in TR06) |
| 19 | **type** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>1 (0x1): solid<br/>2 (0x2): knockable</details> | Object behaviour (NFS2 SE: nfs2sen.exe 0x441ec0, 0x435160): knockable (2) is knocked away when hit at abs(vx) + abs(vz) >= 11 m/s and stops being solid then; every other value is solid. The NFS2 and NFS2 SE tracks have 1 and 2 only |
### **RoadVectorsExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Orientation of the road surface: normal + forward vectors pair. Referenced by index from polygon_map records ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **normal** | 6 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 15 bits is a fractional part, normalized | A normal vector of the road surface |
| 6 | **forward** | 6 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 16-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 15 bits is a fractional part, normalized | A forward vector of the road (direction of the track) |
### **CollisionExtraDataRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 36 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A point of the track collision spline (road centre line) with road orientation vectors and distances to the road borders, 8 points per track block. These are the track slices the car physics walks: NFS2 SE keeps the array at `DAT_004dec18` (count `DAT_004dec10`, 0x24 bytes per record) and finds the slice of a car as the one with the nearest centre by xz distance (nfs2sen.exe 0x439470) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **position** | 12 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | A global position of track collision spline point (slice centre). The unit is meter |
| 12 | **normal** | 3 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 8-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 7 bits is a fractional part, normalized | A normal vector of road surface. NFS2 SE reads each signed byte as `value << 9` (16.16) |
| 15 | **forward** | 3 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 8-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 7 bits is a fractional part, normalized | A forward vector, read like `normal` |
| 18 | **right** | 3 | Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 8-bit real number (little-endian, signed), where last 7 bits is a fractional part, normalized | A right vector, read like `normal` |
| 21 | **unk0** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 22 | **block_idx** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the TRK block (chunk) this point belongs to (NFS2 SE: nfs2sen.exe 0x438f90, 0x4395c0) |
| 24 | **unk1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
| 26 | **left_border** | 2 | 16-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Distance to left track border in meters (NFS2 SE reads it as `value * 0x100`, 16.16). The NFS2 SE physics takes the larger of the two borders (nfs2sen.exe 0x441720) |
| 28 | **right_border** | 2 | 16-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Distance to right track border in meters, read like `left_border` |
| 30 | **flags** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Two 4-bit wall types (NFS2, NFS2 SE: 0x11, 0x44, 0x22 most often): high nibble the left road edge, low nibble the right one. NFS2 SE (nfs2sen.exe 0x458650): 0 = no wall on that side, otherwise the car hits a wall at `left_border` / `right_border` (0.25 m inside) and the nibble becomes its crash type; 6 = a car more than 3 m above the ground gets a tumble kick instead; 7 = a fast car is thrown up (tracks 6 and 7 only, switched off in the shipped game). When either nibble is 2 the vertical dynamics (newton, 0x44e170) treat the slice as having a ceiling: a car more than 10 m above the ground hits it |
| 31 | **lanes** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>4-bits int "unk"<br/>4-bits int "count" | Low nibble `count`: the slice's lane count. The NFS2 SE start grid (car start position, nfs2sen.exe 0x43ea40) puts the cars (count / 2) lane widths (`left_lane_width` / `right_lane_width`) from the centre, only on tracks whose grid side flag is set. High nibble `unk` unknown. Always 0 in the NFS3 files |
| 32 | **left_lane_width** | 1 | 8-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 1 bits is a fractional part | Lane width on the left side in meters, unit 0.5 m: NFS2 SE reads it as `value << 15` (16.16; start grid, nfs2sen.exe 0x43ea40). The NFS3 files have other values here (over the whole byte range), meaning unknown |
| 33 | **right_lane_width** | 1 | 8-bit real number (little-endian, not signed), where last 1 bits is a fractional part | Lane width on the right side in meters, read like `left_lane_width`. The NFS3 files have other values here (over the whole byte range), meaning unknown |
| 34 | **unk3** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Unknown purpose |
### **ColPolygon** ###
#### **Size**: 8 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A single polygon of terrain or prop ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **texture** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Texture number. It is not a number of texture in QFS file. Instead, it is an index of mapping entry in corresponding COL file, which contains real texture number |
| 2 | **texture2** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | 255 (texture number for the other side == none ?) |
| 4 | **vertices** | 4 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Polygon vertices (indexes from vertex table). NFS2 SE reads them at bytes +4..+7 of TRK road polygons (nfs2sen.exe 0x439130, 0x439200) |
## **Images** ##
### **EacImage** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>64 (0x40): 4Bit PS1<br/>96 (0x60): DXT1 compressed bitmap<br/>97 (0x61): DXT3 compressed bitmap<br/>98 (0x62): DXT5 compressed bitmap<br/>109 (0x6d): 16Bit_4444 color format bitmap<br/>120 (0x78): 16Bit_0565 color format bitmap<br/>121 (0x79): 4Bit (swapped)<br/>122 (0x7a): 4Bit<br/>123 (0x7b): 8Bit<br/>125 (0x7d): 32Bit color format bitmap<br/>126 (0x7e): 16Bit_1555 color format bitmap<br/>127 (0x7f): 24Bit color format bitmap</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of the image to the first block attached to it: the palette of an 8Bit image, hot spots (0x7C), text (0x6F), and in NFS6 0x69 / 0x70 blocks. Every attached block starts with its id and the offset to the next one (0 in the last), so they make a chain, which this parser follows. 0 when nothing is attached (then an 8Bit image uses !pal or !PAL of the SHPI), never the size of the image block. Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field is attached. TNFS has other values in a few car (CFM) and track (FAM) textures without attached blocks: mostly a negative offset to the !PAL item of the SHPI, sometimes garbage |
| 4 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap width in pixels |
| 6 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap height in pixels |
| 8 | **pivot** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | TNFS dashboards add both coordinates to the points of `hot_spots`. y coordinate is used by the horizon bitmap "horz" of TNFS FAM files when the game scrolls it (horizon "ring type" 0, the open road tracks by default): this row of the bitmap lies on the horizon line (Win95 SE FUN_0043ae64). The horizon ring (ring type 1, the closed tracks) does not use it |
| 12 | **position** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bitmap position on screen. Used for menu/dash sprites. In NFS5 FSH files this is the position of the image in a texture page (atlas), which is used by CRP models: 12 lower bits of each coordinate are a signed value, 4 higher bits of y are the amount of `mipmaps` levels (always all of them down to 1x1, 0 without mipmaps), set on save |
| 16 | **bitmap** | width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Bytes | Pixel color table. For 8Bit bitmap each value represents an index of color in the attached palette. Palette can be stored: <br/>- right after 8Bit image<br/>- as !pal/!PAL in the same SHPI<br/>- in a different SHPI before this one (if it is WWWW archive)<br/>- even in different QFS file (TNFS, CONTROL directory).<br/>Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md). DXT1/DXT3/DXT5 bitmaps are S3TC-compressed 4x4 pixel blocks (8, 16 and 16 bytes per block) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **mipmaps** | 0..(1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | Optional (if dimensions are powers of two and position.y has the amount of levels): Bytes | Mipmaps pixel data in the same format as `bitmap` field. There are images with sizes w/2 x h/2, w/4 x h/4, .... up to 1x1, in descending order, each padded with zeros to 16 bytes. Only NFS5 files have them: the 4 high bits of `position.y` hold the amount of levels |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness | **pad** | 0..up to offset next_offset | Optional (if next_offset points past the pixels): Padding bytes | Bytes between the pixels (and mipmaps) and the first attached block: zeros, or leftovers aligning it |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness + (1/4 + 1/16 + 1/64 + etc) \* width \* height \* pixel_byteness + up to offset next_offset | **embedded_palette** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has a palette here): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | Embedded palette, which should be assigned to this bitmap (except for ga00 in TR2_001.FAM) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the embedded palette and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x7C here): [ShpiHotSpots](#shpihotspots) | Hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap, read by TNFS dashboards |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **hot_spots_pad** | 0..up to the next attached block | Optional (if the next attached block is 0x7C or 0x6F, not right here): Bytes | Bytes between the hot spots and the next attached block |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **text** | 0..? | Optional (if the chain of attached blocks has 0x6F here): [ShpiText](#shpitext) | Shpi text |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_2** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | A palette after the last attached block, which no block links to (some textures of TNFS TR* tracks) |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_3** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
| 16 + width \* height \* pixel_byteness..? | **embedded_palette_4** | 0..? | Optional (if palette header after the end of the chain): [EacPalette](#eacpalette) | One more palette which no block links to |
### **EacPalette** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Resource with colors LUT (look-up table). EA 8-bit bitmaps have 1-byte value per pixel, meaning the index of color in LUT of assigned palette. Has special colors: 255th in most cases means transparent color, 254th in TNFS car textures is replaced by tail light color, 250th - 253th are the cop car light bar (TNFS maps them to the VGA palette entries 0xFA - 0xFD: red, dark red, blue, dark blue, swapped every 16 clock ticks during a police chase, Win95 SE `gfx_draw_car_model` 0x458d4c) and are rendered black in other cars. The converter writes these colors to `car_colors.json` next to the PNGs.<br/>TNFS car models (CFM) have a second palette `!xxx` next to `!PAL` in the high-poly textures SHPI (TRAFFC in both): the car's slice of the shared 256-color VGA palette in 8-bit modes (Win95 SE `gfx_car_palettes_setup` 0x4572e0). Its first 23 colors (8 for traffic, 24 for the player in a single race / tournament) go to the car's palette entries (player 0x30, opponent 0x48, traffic 0x60 + 8 * slot), then the textures are remapped from `!PAL` to the nearest colors of the VGA palette. `!PAL` is the palette of the textures, `!xxx` is never used to draw them. Cops get none, and the `M*.CFM` models (opponents of a single race / tournament, which share `CARFAMS/CARPAL.FSH` instead) have junk there. Many `!xxx` have the 8-bit bitmap id 0x7B (256x1 or 256x3) instead of a palette id. The converter writes its used colors to `car_colors.json` (`palette_slice`) instead of a file of its own ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>34 (0x22): 24BitDos color format palette<br/>36 (0x24): 24Bit color format palette<br/>41 (0x29): 16Bit_0565 color format palette<br/>42 (0x2a): 32Bit color format palette<br/>45 (0x2d): 16Bit_1555 color format palette</details> | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | When attached to a bitmap: offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows. 0 in palette items (`!pal`) |
| 4 | **num_colors** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of colors |
| 6 | **unk1** | 2 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 8 | **num_colors1** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Equals to num_colors, except for some CRP structures in NFS5 |
| 10 | **unk2** | 6 | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
| 16 | **colors** | ? | Type according to enum `resource_id`:<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 3 bytes<br/>Item type: 3-bytes unsigned integer (big endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>- Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Colors LUT. Color model is selected according to `resource_id` field. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md) |
### **ShpiHotSpots** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A list of hot spots: points of interest of the bitmap it is attached to (after the bitmap and its embedded palette), the index of a point gives its meaning. Many bitmaps of menus, track (FAM) and car (CFM) textures have an empty list, others in the same files have none, and 1x1 placeholder bitmaps of dashboards have copies of the list of another bitmap. TNFS reads it in the dashboard loader only (DOS `tnfs_dash_000522be`, Win95 SE FUN_0041f9a0, the demo `tnfs_dashboard_load`; PSX and 3DO do not read FSH dashboards), from four bitmaps of `SIMDATA/DASH/*DH.FSH` / `*DL.FSH`:<br/>- `dash`: 10 points. 0, 1 = top left and bottom right corners of the rear-view mirror; 2 = radar detector power light; 3..7 = the 5 radar detector level lights; 8, 9 = the loader turns them into offsets from 2 and 3, nothing reads them<br/>- `tach`: tachometer needle tip at 0, 1024, 2048... RPM (the needle is interpolated between them), the last point is the needle centre<br/>- `sped`: speedometer needle tip at 0, 10, 20... mph (0, 20, 40... km/h in the German version), the last point is the needle centre. The cars with a digital speedometer draw digits instead<br/>- `gate`: gear lever knob position for every gear: 0 = reverse, 1 = neutral, then gears from 1st: 7 or 8 points. The game reads 9 points (a 9th, where present, is at the corner of the bitmap)<br/>The game walks the attached blocks until it finds 0x7C, so it hangs when one of these bitmaps has no hot spots ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x7c | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **num_points** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of points array |
| 8 | **points** | num_points\*8 | Array of `num_points` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Points in screen pixels, relative to the bitmap: the screen point is `position` + `pivot` + point, so `pivot` + point is the pixel of the bitmap. TNFS reads the low byte of the amount only |
### **ShpiText** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Text attached to an SHPI image. In the NFS3 / NFS4 sky archives (`SKY.FSH`, `sky.qfs`) the `SUN*` images carry the sun sprite settings: the numbers after `A` (azimuth, degrees), `B` and `R` (the sprite's corners are 10 * R from its centre) and the words `ROTATE`, `NOADD` (not additive), `INFRONT` (drawn after the clouds) (nfs3.exe 0x47a970, nfs4.exe 0x4c9050, which reads it only when `Tr.ini` has no `hasSun=1`). Elsewhere the purpose is unclear ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x6f | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of this block to the next block attached to the same bitmap (0 when this is the last one). Recomputed on save when a block parsed into a field follows |
| 4 | **len_text** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of 'text' utf8 block |
| 8 | **text** | len_text | UTF-8 string | Text contents |
## **Fonts** ##
### **FfnFont** ###
#### **Size**: 48..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Bitmap font: a font atlas bitmap plus glyph definitions (position and size of each symbol in the atlas) and optional kerning table ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. One of ['"FNTF"', '"FNTP"', '"FNTS"', '"FNTX"', '"FNTM"', '"FNTG"', '"FNTA"', '"FntF"', '"FntP"', '"FntS"', '"FntX"', '"FntM"', '"FntG"', '"FntA"'] | Resource ID |
| 4 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this FFN block in bytes. Does not include the embedded palette of an 8Bit bitmap (and padding to it after bitmap data); the palette of a 4Bit bitmap (NFS6) is included. For older versions (I set version <= 101, but it can be anywhere up to < 309), "padding_2" length not included as well |
| 8 | **version** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Font format version. Defines the layout of glyph definitions (see [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition)): 11 bytes below 200, 12 bytes up to 309 (last one padding), 12 bytes with `num_kern` above 309, 16 bytes from 321 with the `format` flag 16-bytes. Changing it changes the size of every glyph definition. Game fonts: 100 / 101 (TNFS to NFS4), 309 to 366 (NFS6) |
| 10 | **num_glyphs** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of symbols, defined in this font |
| 12 | **flags** | 4 | Sub-byte compound block (little endian):<br/>13-bits int "pad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: 12-bytes<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: 16-bytes<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: ASCII<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Unicode<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Shift-JIS<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Reserved<br/>4-bits int "layoutpad"<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: LTR<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: RTL<br/>1-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Horizontal<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Vertical<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: Roman (english)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: Ideographic (Kanji)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: Hanging (Arabic)<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: Unknown<br/>4-bits int "drawpad"<br/>1-bit flag "vram"<br/>1-bit flag "outline"<br/>1-bit flag "dropshadow"<br/>1-bit flag "antialiased" | Font flags: format of glyph definitions, encoding, layout and draw attributes |
| 16 | **center** | 2 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 1-byte unsigned integer | Unknown purpose |
| 18 | **ascent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the top of the glyphs in pixels. `ascent + descent` is the line height, and a glyph is drawn `y_offset` below the top of its line. NFS6 capitals end at `ascent`; TNFS and NFS2 fonts have `descent` 0 and keep the whole line height here |
| 19 | **descent** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the baseline to the bottom of the glyphs in pixels: NFS6 descenders end at `ascent + descent` |
| 20 | **definitions_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to definitions block |
| 24 | **kernings_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to kernings. 0 if there is no kernings table |
| 28 | **bdata_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Pointer to bitmap block |
| 32 | **padding_0** | up to offset definitions_ptr | Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| definitions_ptr | **definitions** | num_glyphs\*11..num_glyphs\*17 | Array of `num_glyphs` items<br/>Item type: [GlyphDefinition](#glyphdefinition) | Definitions of chars in this bitmap font, sorted by `code` (the writer keeps this order, stable sort by `code`) |
| ? | **padding_1** | 0..up to offset kernings_ptr | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Padding bytes | Unknown purpose |
| ? | **kernings** | 0..? | Optional (if kernings_ptr != 0): Array, prefixed with length field<br/>Length field type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian)<br/>Item type: [KerningItem](#kerningitem) | Kerning pairs table. For versions > 309 (glyphs with `num_kern`) the pairs are sorted by right glyph, so the pairs of one right glyph follow each other: the writer keeps this order (stable sort by `right`) |
| ? | **padding_2** | up to offset bdata_ptr | Padding bytes | Puts the bitmap at the offset the game files use: versions < 309 at a multiple of 16 (gap filled with 0xAD; NFS2 SWISS36 at a multiple of 8), newer ones so that the pixels after the 16-byte bitmap header start at a multiple of 128 (gap starts with "Buy ERTS", then zeros). Recomputed on save when the glyph or kerning tables change size, keeping the alignment of the file read |
| bdata_ptr | **bitmap** | 16..? | [EacImage](#eacimage) | Font atlas bitmap data |
| ? | **remaining_bytes** | remaining bytes | Bytes | Unknown purpose |
### **GlyphDefinition** ###
#### **Size**: 11..17 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Glyph definition.<br/>- for FNT version < 200 has length 11 bytes.<br/>- for versions >= 200 and <= 309 - 12 bytes, last byte is padding.<br/>- for versions > 309 - 12th byte is num_kern.<br/>- for versions >= 321 it may be 16 bytes if "format" flag is set to 16-bytes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **code** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of symbol |
| 2 | **width** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Width of symbol in font bitmap |
| 3 | **height** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Height of symbol in font bitmap |
| 4 | **x** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (x) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 6 | **y** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Position (y) of symbol in font bitmap |
| 8 | **advance** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text. 0 in every game font with 16-byte glyphs, which keep it in `x_advance` |
| 9 | **x_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (x) for drawing the character image |
| 10 | **y_offset** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Offset (y) for drawing the character image |
| 11 | **num_kern** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version > 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Number of kerning pairs with this glyph as the right (second) glyph |
| 11..12 | **pad** | 0..1 | Optional (if ^^version <= 309): 1-byte unsigned integer | Padding |
| 11..13 | **kern_index** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the first kerning pair with this glyph as the right glyph: its `num_kern` pairs follow each other in the kerning table from here. 0 if the glyph has no kerning pairs |
| 11..15 | **x_advance** | 0..2 | Optional (if ^^flags/format == 16-bytes): 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Distance from the start of this symbol to the start of the next one in rendered text, for 16-byte glyphs (`advance` is 0 in all of them in the game files) |
### **KerningItem** ###
#### **Size**: 4 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Kerning pair: horizontal adjustment of the gap between two specific glyphs ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **left** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Code of left glyph |
| 2 | **kerning** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Kerning amount in pixels, added to the gap between the glyphs |
| 3 | **right** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Code of right glyph |
## **Audio** ##
### **EaAudioStreams** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A file of EA audio streams (`SCHl`): NFS2 / NFS2 SE `.ASF` (a song), NFS2 / NFS2 SE / NFS3 `.MUS` (interactive music: a stream per node of the `.MAP` file of the same name), NFS4 `Data/Audio/MUSIC/*.ASF`, NFS5 songs in `GameData/Music/zzzymus.viv`, NFS6 `audio/music/*.asf`, NFS6 speech in `radio.viv`. Converted to WAV with FFmpeg: a file with one stream to `<name>.wav` + `<name>.meta.json` (loop), a file with more streams to a folder with `<index>.wav` + `<index>.meta.json` per stream and `playthrough.wav` (the streams in the order of the `.LIN`, else `.MAP` file next to it, see `EaMusicMap`; all streams in file order without one) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **streams** | streams up to the end of file\*12..? | Array of `streams up to the end of file` items<br/>Item type: [EaAudioStream](#eaaudiostream) | Audio streams |
### **EaAudioStream** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA audio stream (NFS2 - NFS6 music, NFS6 speech): header chunk "SCHl" with a sound patch (sampling rate, channels, number of samples, loop, codec), then the wave data in chunks of 8-byte header (id, length including the header) and data: SCCl (amount of SCDl chunks), SCDl (wave data), SCLl (loop end), SCEl (end). Explained by [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`); the converter decodes it with FFmpeg ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SCHl" | Header chunk id |
| 4 | **header_length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Length of the header chunk, including the chunk id and this field |
| 8 | **header** | 4..? | [EaSoundPatch](#easoundpatch) | Sound patch: tags before `info_start` are playback settings, the ones after it describe the wave data. Without the `version` tag (NFS2 - NFS4) `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, no `codec` is 16-bit little endian PCM (NFS3 menu music: each SCDl chunk holds the amount of samples, 4 bytes, then the samples, channels interleaved), the sampling rate is 22050 without `sampling_rate`; with `version` 1 (NFS5, NFS6) the codec is EA-XA ADPCM v2 ("R1" in FFmpeg). `loop_start` / `loop_end` are sample indices of the loop |
| 12..? | **header_padding** | header_length - (header fields length) | Bytes | Zeros up to the end of the header chunk |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length)..? | **data** | chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl | Bytes | Chunks SCCl, SCDl, SCLl, SCEl with the wave data, as they are in the file |
| 12 + header_length - (header fields length) + chunks up to and including the end chunk SCEl..? | **padding** | up to the next stream or the end of file | Bytes | Zeros aligning the next stream of the file to 4 bytes |
### **EaMusicMap** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Interactive music map "PFDx" (EA PathFinder) versions 0 and 1, NFS2 / NFS2 SE `GAMEDATA/AUDIO/PC/*.MAP`, NFS3 `GameData/Audio/pc/*.map` and `*.lin`, for the `.MUS` file of the same name (EaAudioStreams), big endian. NFS3 `.lin` maps list the same streams as the `.map`, with one branch per node (0..100): the song played linearly. Music plays node by node: when a node ends, the branch matching the music state value which the game sets (0..100) picks the next one; a game event jumps to the node `events` gives for the section of the current node. Layout from [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl_map_mpf_mus.c`), the node fields from the files ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "PFDx" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **version** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Version, 0 or 1 |
| 5 | **start_node** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Index of the node the music starts with |
| 6 | **num_nodes** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Amount of nodes |
| 7 | **num_events** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Amount of events per section, 16 in NFS2 SE |
| 8 | **unk0** | 3 | Bytes | Zeros |
| 11 | **num_sections** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Amount of sections (rows of `events`) |
| 12 | **nodes** | num_nodes\*28 | Array of `num_nodes` items<br/>Item type: [EaMusicMapNode](#eamusicmapnode) | Nodes |
| 12 + num_nodes\*28 | **events** | num_sections\*num_events | Array of `num_sections` items<br/>Item size: num_events bytes<br/>Item type: Array of `num_events` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | For each section, the node each game event jumps to (0 for an event without a jump). Meanings of the events are not known |
| 12 + num_nodes\*28 + num_sections\*num_events | **stream_offsets** | num_nodes\*4 | Array of `num_nodes` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of the audio stream of each node in the `.MUS` file |
### **EaMusicMapNode** ###
#### **Size**: 28 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A node of interactive music: one audio stream of the `.MUS` file and the nodes which can follow it ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **section** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Section of the song the node belongs to: the row of `events` used while it plays |
| 1 | **num_branches** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Amount of used `branches`, 0 in an end node |
| 2 | **unk0** | 2 | Bytes | Always FF FF |
| 4 | **branches** | 24 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item type: [EaMusicMapBranch](#eamusicmapbranch) | Branches, the first `num_branches` are used, the next ones are zeros or leftovers. The value ranges of the used ones cover 0..100 |
### **EaMusicMapBranch** ###
#### **Size**: 3 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A branch of an interactive music node: the node to play next while the music state value (0..100) set by the game is in the range ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **min_value** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Lowest state value of the branch |
| 1 | **max_value** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Highest state value of the branch (100 at most) |
| 2 | **next_node** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Index of the node to play next |
### **EaSoundPatch** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: EA sound patch ("PT" header): a sound of a BNKl sound bank as a list of tags. Tags before `info_start` are playback settings (priority, volume, pan, pitch bend range...), tags after it describe the wave data: `num_samples`, `channels` (default 1), `sampling_rate` (default 22050), loop sample indices `loop_start` and `loop_end` (inclusive; a sample loops when it has one of them, from 0 / up to the last sample when the other one is missing), `data_offset` (wave data offset from the start of the bank file) and the codec. Without the `version` tag, `codec` 7 is EA-XA ADPCM v1, 9 is EA MicroTalk 10:1 (speech), no `codec` tag is 16-bit little endian PCM. With `version` 1, `codec_2` 8 is 16-bit little endian PCM, 9 is signed 8-bit PCM, no `codec_2` tag is EA-XA ADPCM v2. Stereo samples are interleaved. A sound can have several layers, played together, separated by the `layer_end` tag, each one with its own settings and wave data (NFS3 player car engines add a short mono loop to the stereo engine sample) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **platform_magic** | 2 | UTF-8 string. Always == "PT" | Patch header magic |
| 2 | **platform** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Platform id, 0 is PC |
| 4 | **tags** | up to and including tag "end"..? | Array of `up to and including tag "end"` items<br/>Item type: [EaSoundPatchTag](#easoundpatchtag) | Tags |
### **EaSoundPatchTag** ###
#### **Size**: 1..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A tag of EA sound patch: tag id, then (except for tags 0xFC-0xFF) the length of the value and the value, big endian unsigned. Tag meanings follow [vgmstream](https://github.com/vgmstream/vgmstream) (`ea_schl.c`), the ones named `unk_*` are not known ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **tag** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>0 (0x0): unk_0x00<br/>6 (0x6): priority<br/>7 (0x7): unk_0x07<br/>8 (0x8): release_envelope<br/>9 (0x9): playback_envelope<br/>10 (0xa): bend_range_semitones<br/>11 (0xb): bank_channels<br/>12 (0xc): pan<br/>13 (0xd): random_pan_range<br/>14 (0xe): volume<br/>15 (0xf): random_volume_range<br/>16 (0x10): detune<br/>17 (0x11): random_detune_range<br/>18 (0x12): unk_0x12<br/>19 (0x13): effect_bus<br/>20 (0x14): user_data<br/>128 (0x80): version<br/>130 (0x82): channels<br/>131 (0x83): codec<br/>132 (0x84): sampling_rate<br/>133 (0x85): num_samples<br/>134 (0x86): loop_start<br/>135 (0x87): loop_end<br/>136 (0x88): data_offset<br/>137 (0x89): data_offset_channel_2<br/>138 (0x8a): unk_0x8a<br/>139 (0x8b): unk_0x8b<br/>140 (0x8c): flags<br/>145 (0x91): unk_0x91<br/>146 (0x92): unk_0x92<br/>147 (0x93): unk_0x93<br/>160 (0xa0): codec_2<br/>252 (0xfc): padding<br/>253 (0xfd): info_start<br/>254 (0xfe): layer_end<br/>255 (0xff): end</details> | Tag id |
| 1 | **value_length** | 0..1 | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): 1-byte unsigned integer | Length of value in bytes. 0 means value 0 |
| 1..2 | **value** | 0..value_length | Optional (if tag is not padding, info_start, layer_end or end): Bytes | Value, big endian unsigned integer |
## **Misc** ##
### **Nfs2HorizonInfo** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Sky of an NFS2 / NFS2 SE track for the software renderer, `GAMEDATA/TRACKS/PC/TR<nn>.HRZ` (nfs2sen.exe `c:\nfs2se\game\vga\hrzsku.c` builds the name `%sTr%02d.hrz`). Text with C comments, 26 numbers named by the comments of the files: black horizon flag, mirror flag, radius, rotation angle in degrees, distance for the flat projection (<= radius), base y of the flat shaded area (world offset), height of the horizon (offset from base), pixmap base (percentage of the height), flat shaded sky colour (r, g, b), horizon base colour, 4 depth cueing distances (0..1100), 4 depth cueing light values (0..15), colour system (0 rgb, 1 hsv) and a colour. The converter reads these names from the comments only: the software renderer is not ported, so this file does not make a sky texture ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **text** | the whole file | UTF-8 string | The settings text: C comments (`/* ... */`) and comma separated numbers |
